claims.text: Damaged H13 hot-work die steel is sensitive to hot cracking when repaired by traditional fusion welding.

Laser cladding a high-entropy-alloy coating onto H13 steel using an Inconel 718 transition layer will improve surface integrity and reduce cracking relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface.
The proposed coating system will improve wear resistance.
The proposed coating system will improve corrosion resistance.
The proposed coating system will increase resistance to plastic deformation.
An Inconel 718 transition layer produces strong bonding between the H13 substrate and the high-entropy-alloy coating.
Inconel 718 provides excellent thermal-expansion matching in this coating system.
The Inconel 718 transition layer provides strong stress resistance.
The Inconel 718 transition layer reduces interfacial cracking under bending load.
Laser cladding creates a metallurgical bond and a controlled interfacial microstructure.
The Inconel 718 layer facilitates adequate element diffusion at the interface.
The Inconel 718 layer reduces stress concentrations at the coating–substrate interface.
Improved interfacial bonding and reduced stress concentration improve load transfer.
Traditional fusion-welding repairs tend to develop hot cracks because of thermal gradients.
The laser-clad specimens will exhibit fewer surface and interfacial cracks under both bending and hot-tensile loading than fusion-welded and untreated H13 specimens.
The laser-clad specimens will have higher yield strength than fusion-welded and untreated H13 specimens.
The method is effective for H13 steel under high thermal and mechanical loads.
The method is applicable to die-casting or hot-stamping service.
Performance on other substrate materials or under radically different service conditions is unverified.
Reproducibility across laser-cladding parameters and long-term bond stability under cyclic or environmental aging remain uncertain.

contradictions.description: The conditions field describes hot-tensile and three-point-bending conditions as processing conditions under which the repair is performed, whereas the experiment treats them as post-deposition mechanical tests.
